options: Total bytes moved divided by total FLOPs performed
Total FLOPs performed divided by total bytes moved from memory
The number of threads divided by the number of SMs
Clock speed multiplied by core count
questions.explain: Arithmetic intensity is FLOPs performed divided by bytes moved from memory — a measure of how much math is done per byte of data.

questions.q: A kernel has low arithmetic intensity. What limits its performance?
options: The GPU's peak compute throughput
Memory bandwidth, regardless of how many cores are idle
The number of registers per thread
The clock speed of the CPU host
questions.explain: Low arithmetic intensity means the kernel moves a lot of data relative to the math performed on it, making it memory-bound and capped by bandwidth.

questions.q: Why is general matrix multiplication (GEMM) typically compute-bound?
options: It never reads from global memory
It reuses each loaded value many times across the multiply-accumulate pattern, giving it high arithmetic intensity
It only runs on the CPU
It has no floating-point operations
questions.explain: GEMM's multiply-accumulate pattern reuses loaded values repeatedly, producing high arithmetic intensity and typically a compute-bound profile.

questions.q: In the roofline model, what does the 'ridge point' represent?
options: The maximum clock speed of the GPU
The arithmetic intensity at which a kernel transitions from memory-bound to compute-bound
The point where a kernel crashes due to out-of-memory
The number of SMs on the device
questions.explain: The ridge point is where the memory-bandwidth ceiling and the compute-throughput ceiling intersect, marking the switch between memory-bound and compute-bound regimes.

questions.q: An elementwise operation like ReLU reads one value, applies one operation, and writes one value back. Why is this typically memory-bound?
options: Because its arithmetic intensity is close to 1 — very little math is done per byte moved
Because ReLU requires double-precision floating point
Because elementwise operations cannot run on a GPU
Because it uses Tensor Cores exclusively
questions.explain: With roughly one operation per byte read and written, elementwise ops have arithmetic intensity near 1, placing them firmly in the memory-bound region.
